questions.q: In var category = request.queryParams.category;, what is category when the caller sends no ?category= at all?
options: undefined
An empty GlideRecord object
The string "null"
The request is automatically rejected with a 400
questions.explain: An unsent query parameter simply reads as undefined — the script has to check for that before using it in a query, as the lesson's example does.

questions.q: An Equipment API defines GET /{sys_id}, GET /, POST /, and PUT /{sys_id} under one base path. How are these actually structured?
options: As four separate Resource records, each with its own script, sharing one base path
As one Resource whose single script branches on request.httpMethod
As four separate sys_ws_definition records, one per method
They cannot share a base path and must each define their own
questions.explain: Each path-and-method combination is its own Resource record with its own focused script, not a branch inside a single script.

questions.q: A Resource script returns response.setStatus(400) when request.body.data.asset_tag is missing. What is 400 signaling, as opposed to 404 or 500?
options: That the caller's request itself was malformed or incomplete, not that the server failed or a record was missing
That the record was found but is read-only
That the server experienced an internal failure unrelated to the request
That the requested record does not exist
questions.explain: 400 means the request itself is bad (missing required data) — distinct from 404 (not found) and 500 (server-side failure).

questions.q: Where is a Scripted REST API's required-roles setting actually configured, and when is it checked relative to a Resource's script?
options: On the API definition itself, checked before any Resource's script runs
Inside each Resource's script, using gs.hasRole() as the first line
On the underlying table's ACL, checked after the script finishes
It isn't configurable — role checks always happen only in GlideRecord calls inside the script
questions.explain: The required-roles setting lives on the sys_ws_definition record itself and is evaluated by the platform before any Resource script executes.

questions.q: A caller lacking the role required on a Scripted REST API's definition sends a request. What happens?
options: They never reach the Resource's script — the platform rejects the call with an authorization failure first
The script runs normally, and setStatus(403) must be called manually inside it
The request is silently logged but still returns a 200 with an empty body
Table ACLs are checked instead, and the API-level role requirement is ignored
questions.explain: The API-level role requirement is the first gate — it keeps the entire API unreachable to the wrong caller before any script code executes.
